messages.content:
You are a helpful language model tasked with rewriting a given text to convey specific emotional tones. For each emotion listed below, rewrite the original sentence as if you were the speaker and wanted to express that specific emotion. Focus on minimal but effective changes to convey the tone without altering the core meaning or structure of the sentence. Ensure the rewritten sentences remain concise and aligned with the original text.

Emotions to rewrite for:
- Joy
- Sadness
- Fear
- Anger
- Surprise
- Disgust

Please rewrite the text for each emotion. Do not extend or shorten the text unnecessarily.
I was in the same outfit as at the party, with the addition of a voice changing microphone under the mask and a glow stick that I stuck in there to try to illuminate my eyes a bit.

output.original_text: I was in the same outfit as at the party, with the addition of a voice changing microphone under the mask and a glow stick that I stuck in there to try to illuminate my eyes a bit.
output.joy: I was in the same outfit as at the party, and I added a fun voice changing microphone under the mask along with a glow stick to brighten my eyes a bit!
output.sadness: I was in the same outfit as at the party, but this time I added a voice changing microphone under the mask and a glow stick to make my eyes look a bit more alive...
output.fear: I was in the same outfit as at the party, and I added a voice changing microphone under the mask and a glow stick, hoping it would help me seem less invisible in the dark.
output.anger: I was in the same outfit as at the party, and I had to shove a voice changing microphone under the mask along with a glow stick just to get some light in my eyes!
output.surprise: I was in the same outfit as at the party, but then I added a voice changing microphone under the mask and a glow stick to light up my eyes a bit—it turned out surprisingly fun!
output.disgust: I was in the same outfit as at the party, but I shoved a voice changing microphone under the mask and a glow stick in there, trying to illuminate my eyes—it felt so tacky.
